title: Ignore the noise — and rescue a file you already tracked
summary: Build a .gitignore that hides build output and secrets, then handle the case everyone hits: a file that .gitignore refuses to ignore because it is already tracked.
mental_model: gitignore only decides whether git *starts* tracking a file. Once a file is tracked, gitignore is ignored. Untrack it first, then the rule applies.
danger: `git rm --cached .env` removes the file from git but leaves it on disk — and it stays in every past commit. Ignoring a secret after committing it does not un-leak it.

steps.title: See the noise
steps.why: Five untracked files, only one of which anyone wants in history. Untracked noise is not harmless — it hides the files you actually meant to add.

steps.title: Write the ignore rules
steps.why: `*.log` matches at every depth. A trailing slash means 'directory'. A leading `!` negates a previous rule, which is how you keep one file inside an ignored directory.

write.content:
# build output
build/
!build/keep.md

# logs and scratch files, at any depth
*.log
*.tmp

# never commit secrets
.env

steps.expect: Only .gitignore and build/keep.md remain untracked — and .env is still listed, which is the lesson.

steps.title: Ask git why a file is ignored
steps.why: `check-ignore -v` prints the file, line number and pattern responsible. Guessing at gitignore behaviour is a waste of an afternoon; this command answers it outright.
commands: git check-ignore -v debug.log src/trace.log build/output.bin notes.tmp
steps.expect: Each file mapped to the exact .gitignore line that catches it.

steps.title: The negation that does not work by accident
steps.why: `build/` excludes the whole directory, so git never looks inside it — and `!build/keep.md` cannot rescue a file from a directory git skipped. The fix is to ignore the *contents*, not the directory.

write.content:
# build output, but keep the notes
build/*
!build/keep.md

# logs and scratch files, at any depth
*.log
*.tmp

# never commit secrets
.env

steps.expect: build/keep.md is now untracked-and-addable; check-ignore reports nothing for it.

steps.title: The file gitignore will not ignore
steps.why: `.env` is already tracked from the setup commit, so the rule has no effect. This is the single most common gitignore complaint, and the answer is always the same: untrack it.
steps.expect: 'rm .env' staged as a deletion, and .env disappears from the untracked list because now the rule applies.

steps.title: Commit the cleanup
steps.why: The commit records two things: the ignore rules, and the fact that .env is no longer tracked. The file itself is untouched on disk — `--cached` only removes it from the index.
commands: git commit -m "Ignore build output, logs and secrets"

verify.label: …but the file is still on disk, because --cached only touches the index
build/keep.md was rescued from the ignored directory
verify.hint: ignore build/* rather than build/, then negate with !build/keep.md

verify.label: no logs, scratch files or build output got committed

pitfalls: A tracked file ignores .gitignore entirely. `git rm --cached <file>` is the fix.
`build/` and `build/*` behave differently the moment you want to negate something inside. Use `build/*` when you need an exception.
Committing a secret then ignoring it leaves the secret in history. Rotate the key — a rewrite alone is not enough once it has been pushed.
Personal noise (editor swap files, .DS_Store) belongs in `core.excludesfile` globally, not in a shared project's .gitignore.
